2026-07-17-dive-radio-bumpy-takeoff|drop.summary: The hosts own up to first-show jank — a botched AI intro video, a rushed brand refresh — and welcome viewers to the first, admittedly bumpy, Dive Radio livestream.
Industry-news riffing: the hosts react to designer moves — big names leaving for Cursor — and debate whether running design at a fast-scaling company is a job anyone should want.
Wind-down talk at the very end: the hosts trade late-night work-habit confessions — chasing an idea until early morning — and joke that none of it should be taken as advice.

2026-07-23-dive-radio-data-vs-intuition-.summary: A portfolio showcase: one host screen-shares designer Sid's playful, personal portfolio and tells how he found him through the talent network, while the audience vote gets set up.
Recorded community nominations play back to back: a nominee signs off by nominating another designer, and the hosts riff on the videos' one-liners and self-edited craft between clips.
The hosts read through a community write-up on what design engineering actually is, recommend it on screen, then turn it into a debate about where designers should position themselves.

2026-07-30-dive-radio-mixed-media-workfl.summary: The nomination chain continues — a recorded video hands the torch to an engineer at Resend — and the hosts talk about how the pay-it-forward format started and why it is becoming their favorite segment.

A talk stretch on AI demo overload: the hosts argue the viral demos are really experiments in chaining tools together — mixed-media workflows — not finished products, and that people judge them wrong.
A live gameplay demo, music and all: one host plays an AI-built game on screen — running out of missiles, fumbling a landing — while framing it as a playable experiment, not a market-ready game.
The maker explains an AI catching its own broken model — the mesh was unworkable vector soup — and re-meshing it, then walks through the wiki-fed critic agent they use to gate what counts as good.

2026-08-06-dive-radio-backyard-designers.summary: A recorded nomination praising a jaw-dropping WebGL demo wraps up, and the hosts riff on the double nomination and how comforting it is to hear a master admit he didn't know how he pulled it off.

The backyard-project team gets candid about the launch: feedback lists and voice notes pouring in unprompted, the game becoming something they never set out to make, and asking designers what would help.

One of the makers screen-shares a story deck generated by voice with an AI design tool reading the game's own codebase — built in the final hours before the show — and tests whether its images stay consistent.

2026-08-13-dive-radio-goodbye-blank-canv.summary: A recorded nomination from designer James McDonald plays, and one host detours into a family story about everyone imitating James's accent for a week while editing his podcast episode.
The hosts scroll a community pile-on: replies roasting an AI-generated design post, delete-this jokes included, while they debate how seriously to take the backlash.

Show-and-tell of a community-made card game site: the hosts admire its productized admin flow — drag a card and it deploys — until the site's autoplaying music derails the segment and they close the tab.
A guest walks through how their prototyping workflow changed — from making messes on top of the production codebase to isolated quick mockups — and shares a screen of the new setup.
